calls.reason: ARC baselines score poorly, but the syntax study finds successful generalization that varies by training. These limited tests do not settle the broad claim about acquiring sufficiently general abstractions.

Compositional and reversal experiments show generalization failures, but Abacus models extrapolate to six times the training length. The mixed evidence and undefined distance threshold leave the full claim unclear.

Crunchbase reports sharply increased financing in early 2026; Reuters documents infrastructure share declines tied to financing concerns. Neither establishes an industry collapse caused by outlier limitations, and no deadline was given.

Haley and Soloway documented extrapolation failures in 1992. GSM-Plus found recurring robustness weaknesses across 25 models in 2024, supporting the claim that difficulties persisted without implying no improvement.
Xu and colleagues find both extrapolation limits and successes depending on architecture, features and training coverage. Their results do not isolate localism as the general cause Marcus asserts.

Dziri documents multiplication failures beyond training splits, but Jelassi shows sparse-example generalization and Gambardella finds answer-prefix effects. Errors are established; the claimed explanation remains uncertain.
